schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: WITH CTE AS ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID, SALE_DATE FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) SELECT CTE.PRODUCT_ID AS PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME AS PRODUCT_NAME FROM CTE LEFT JOIN PRODUCT P ON CTE.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses an INNER JOIN, which will only return products that have sales within the specified date range. On the other hand, Q2 uses a LEFT JOIN, which will return all products, even if they do not have sales within the specified date range. The difference arises when there are products in the PRODUCT table that do not have any sales records in the SALES table.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should include products that have sales within the date range and products that do not have any sales records. The difference in results will be observed when running Q1 and Q2 on this test data.
